newsitem.title: UK: HK's Lee wants Britain to put pressure on China.
newsitem.headline: HK's Lee wants Britain to put pressure on China.

text.p: Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Martin Lee on Tuesday called on Britain's new Labour government to make sure Beijing did not violate human rights after taking over the colony next month.

Lee, who is due to meet Prime Minister Tony Blair and Foreign Secretary Robin Cook on Wednesday, said he would protest about what he said were violations of the 1984 treaty under which Britain agreed to hand over Hong Kong.

Lee, who has consistently maintained that Beijing will clamp down on the colony once it takes control on June 30, accused the outgoing Conservative administration of turning a blind eye to Beijing's acts.
"I hope the new Labour government will do something," said Lee, head of the colony's Democratic Party.
"When there is a will, there are many options. When there is no will, there are many excuses. I hope Labour don't simply blame the Conservative government," he told a news conference.

Pro-democracy activists oppose China's plans to replace the colony's elected legislature with one carefully crafted by Beijing, which they says flies in the face of the 1984 Sino-British Joint Declaration.
"These things are already happening but I don't see the British government doing anything about it," Lee said.

"The problem we're facing has very much been brought about by the neglect of the British government over many years," he said, accusing the Conservatives of keeping quiet in return for British firms signing big contracts.

Tung Chee-hwa, the man Beijing has chosen to lead the colony, vows there will be no violent crackdown once he takes over but has already unveiled plans to amend laws on political funding and public demonstrations.

Lee says this represents a clear threat to freedom of speech and he is also unhappy that the Beijing-dominated provisional legislature, which will take over from July 1, has already begun debating laws.

"This body is illegally attempting to debate legislation before July 1," he said. "Any bill it passes is liable to be successfully challenged in the Hong Kong Supreme Court...it's like asking a baby to crawl before it's been born."
The Democratic Party holds the largest number of seats in the current legislature but none in the provisional council.
